title: Separate public Problem from hidden suite
why: Players see the statement and examples. The server keeps the Hidden suite sealed. A leak breaks fairness.
outcome: Validate bank input and project only public fields.

steps.title: Two views of one Problem
steps.question: What may the browser receive?
explanation: A Problem is a coding task with a statement, examples, constraints, and starter code per language. The reference supports C++, Python, and C.
The browser may receive title, description, examples, starters, and visible tests. It must never receive hidden cases, answers, weights, or private paths.
You need this now because Run uses visible cases while Submit later uses the Hidden suite.

title: Call Judge through a small port
why: Game code must request execution without running player code itself. A fake Judge makes this safe to learn.
outcome: Define RunRequest and RunResult, call a fake Judge, and handle success and infrastructure error.

steps.title: A port separates Game from execution
steps.question: What does Judge = { run(request): Promise<result> } mean?
explanation: Judge is a boundary. The Game sends a RunRequest with code, language, and visible cases. The Judge later returns a RunResult. The Game never executes player code directly.
This is dependency injection again: pass one Judge object into the caller. Real Nest decorators come later in M06. Mock Judge examples here never count as real Judge evidence.

vocabulary.meaning: Provider-side execution of one Evaluation. Only the durable Evaluation outcome changes Match state.

steps.title: See start, waiting, settled
steps.question: What does await do?
explanation: Call starts and waits. await pauses your function until the Promise resolves or rejects, then continues. A resolved verdict can still report failure: a wrong answer (passed false), a compile_error, or a runtime_error. Only a broken worker rejects with an infrastructure error. Tests must clean up on every path.

title: Run visible cases without changing score
why: Run is a neutral check against visible examples only. It never touches the Hidden suite and never changes the score.

steps.title: Run versus Submit
steps.question: What does Run change?
explanation: Nothing about score. Run checks current code against visible examples. Submit sends a solution for Hidden suite evaluation and locks it.
You need Run now because players iterate with it during CODING before they ever submit.

vocabulary.meaning: A neutral check against visible examples. Never changes score or touches hidden tests.

explanation: Editor source plus visible cases go to the Judge. Results return with a status: ok, compile_error, or runtime_error. Score stays at its old value on every verdict. Only a broken worker rejects, which the caller records as an infrastructure error without touching the score.
